To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the aquatic invertebrate communities of a reservoir and its tributary stream overlap in the ecotone along the edges of the two water bodies and that the ecotone acts like a semi-permeable membrane to the stream invertebrates.
the aquatic ecotone in this study is an important area for conservation of aquatic fauna and flora.
the main aquatic ecotonic area is the edge ecotones between the open reservoir, sheltered edges of the reservoir and stream, and the main stream.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new concept in conservation, the aquatic ecotone.
the conservation of biodiversity and its management.
the aquatic ecotone, its faunal characteristics and its significance in terms of biodiversity and conservation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the aquatic ecotone is an important feature in the management of water resources and should be considered in conservation planning.
the edge ecotones are the most important areas for conservation, and that the open areas of the main stream or reservoir are less important.
the aquatic ecotone is a significant feature in conservation and that its importance has not been previously appreciated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ecotone between stream and reservoir is not the mouth of the tributary but the edge of the reservoir, and the centre of the reservoir is not the centre of the system.
‘the edge is the place’.
‘the ecotone is the system’.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aquatic communities can be very different from what you would expect from a simple visual assessment.
the ecotone is the most significant part of a multi-system, and should be the focus of management and conservation.
aquatic ecotones are not always where they appear to be.
